title: Faithfully flat finite-presentation algebras admit a finitely presented integer model
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. There exist commutative rings $C,D$ and homomorphisms $C\to A$, $C\to D$, $D\to B$, with the two composites $C\to B$ equal, such that $C$ is of finite presentation over $\mathbf Z$, $D$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation over $C$, and the induced homomorphism $e:A\otimes_C D\to B$, $a\otimes d\mapsto f(a)g(d)$, is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras. Here $f:A\to B$ and $g:D\to B$ are the indicated maps, and the algebra tensor product and induced map are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The rings $C,D$ can be taken in the maximum of the universes of $A,B$.
